questions.questionText: Solve completely the inequality x² − 2x + 3 < 0. Give your answer in interval notation where appropriate.
questions.explanation: The discriminant is negative and the leading coefficient is positive, so the quadratic is always positive.

questions.questionText: Find the stationary points of y=x³−3x²+4x and classify them.
questions.explanation: The discriminant of 3x²−6x+4 is negative, so dy/dx=0 has no real solution.

questions.questionText: Evaluate ∫ x(4+x)² dx.
questions.explanation: Expand to 16x+8x²+x³, then integrate term by term.

questions.questionText: Prove the identity: (1−cos 2θ)/sin 2θ = tan θ, where defined.
questions.explanation: Use 1−cos2θ=2sin²θ and sin2θ=2sinθcosθ. The quotient becomes (2sin²θ)/(2sinθcosθ)=tanθ.

questions.questionText: Let z=6+1i. Find z², |z| and 1/z.
questions.explanation: Use (a+bi)²=(a²−b²)+2abi, |z|=√(a²+b²), and 1/z=(a−bi)/(a²+b²).

questions.questionText: An arithmetic sequence has first term 2 and common difference 4. Derive its nth term and sum of the first n terms.
questions.explanation: Use Tn=a+(n−1)d and Sn=n/2[2a+(n−1)d].

questions.questionText: Find the term independent of x in the expansion of (2x + 1/x)^7.
questions.explanation: Since 7 is odd, the exponent 7−2k can never be zero for integer k.

questions.questionText: Given A=[[4,1],[2,6]], find A⁻¹ and verify AA⁻¹=I.
questions.explanation: det(A)=4×6−2=22; the inverse is (1/det)[[6,−1],[−2,4]]. Multiplication with A gives I.

questions.questionText: Find the equation of the normal to y=x²−2x+4 at x=5.
questions.explanation: Curve gradient is 2x−2=8; normal gradient is −1/8=-0.125. Use point (5,19) to form the line.

questions.questionText: Find the area between y=x² and y=6x for x≥0.
questions.explanation: Intersections are x=0 and x=6. Area=∫₀^6(6x−x²)dx=36.

questions.questionText: Using mathematical induction, prove that 1+2+…+n = n(n+1)/2.
questions.explanation: Base case n=1: 1=1(2)/2. Assume true for n=k. Then 1+…+k+(k+1)=k(k+1)/2+(k+1)=(k+1)(k+2)/2, proving the statement for k+1.

questions.questionText: Find the general solution of dy/dx + 3y = 6e^(−3x).
questions.explanation: The integrating factor is e^(3x). Thus d/dx(ye^(3x))=6; integration gives ye^(3x)=6x+C.

questions.questionText: Find the distance from the point (4,3) to the line 4x + 3y − 12=0.
questions.explanation: Use |Ax₁+By₁+C|/√(A²+B²); the distance is approximately 2.600 units.

questions.questionText: Find dy/dx and the stationary point of y=5ln x−x² for x>0.
questions.explanation: dy/dx=5/x−2x. Setting it to zero gives x²=5/2, so x=√(5/2)≈1.581; substitution gives y≈-0.209.

questions.questionText: Evaluate the infinite geometric series 6 + 6/3 + 6/9 + … and state the condition used.
questions.explanation: Here a=6, r=1/3 and |r|<1. Therefore S∞=a/(1−r)=9.

questions.questionText:
Implicit Differentiation & Normals:
A curve has equation x² + 3xy + 2y² = 12.
(a) Show that dy/dx = -(2x + 3y)/(3x + 4y). [3 marks]
(b) Find the equation of the normal to the curve at the point (2, 1). [3 marks]
questions.explanation:
(a) Differentiate w.r.t. x: 2x + 3y + 3x(dy/dx) + 4y(dy/dx) = 0 -> (3x + 4y)dy/dx = -(2x + 3y) -> dy/dx = -(2x + 3y)/(3x + 4y) [3].
(b) At (2, 1): gradient of tangent = -(4 + 3)/(6 + 4) = -7/10 -> normal gradient = 10/7 [1.5]. Normal: y - 1 = (10/7)(x - 2) -> 7y - 10x + 13 = 0 [1.5].

questions.questionText:
3D Vectors — Lines & Planes:
Line L₁ passes through A(1, -2, 3) with direction d₁ = (2, 1, -1). Plane Π has equation 3x - 2y + z = 14.
(a) Find the coordinates where L₁ intersects plane Π. [4 marks]
(b) Calculate the acute angle between L₁ and plane Π. [3 marks]

First-Order Linear Differential Equations:
Solve the differential equation dy/dx + 2y tan x = sin x, given y = 0 when x = 0, giving y explicitly in terms of cos x. [6 marks]
questions.explanation:
Integrating factor IF = e^(∫ 2 tan x dx) = e^(-2 ln cos x) = sec² x [2].
Multiply through: d/dx(y sec² x) = sin x sec² x = sec x tan x [2].
Integrate: y sec² x = sec x + C. At x=0, y=0 -> 0 = 1 + C -> C = -1 [1].
y = cos² x (sec x - 1) = cos x - cos² x [1].

questions.questionText:
Volume of Revolution:
The finite region bounded by y = √x, the x-axis, and lines x = 1 and x = 4 is rotated through 2π radians about the x-axis. Calculate the exact volume of the solid generated. [4 marks]
questions.explanation: V = π ∫₁⁴ y² dx = π ∫₁⁴ x dx = π [x²/2]₁⁴ = π (8 - 1/2) = (15/2)π cubic units [4].

questions.questionText:
Complex Loci in the Argand Diagram:
On an Argand diagram, sketch and describe the loci satisfying:
(a) |z - (2 - 3i)| = 4 [2 marks]
(b) |z - 1| = |z - 5i| [3 marks]
questions.explanation:
(a) A circle centred at (2, -3) with radius 4 [2].
(b) The perpendicular bisector of the line segment joining (1, 0) and (0, 5): midpoint (1/2, 5/2), slope of join = -5 -> bisector gradient = 1/5 -> y - 2.5 = 0.2(x - 0.5) => 5y = x + 12 [3].

questions.questionText:
Integration by Substitution:
Use the substitution u = 1 + √x (so x = (u - 1)²) to find the exact value of ∫₁⁴ 1 / (1 + √x) dx. [5 marks]

Trigonometric Proofs & Equations:
Prove the identity (sin 3θ / sin θ) - (cos 3θ / cos θ) ≡ 2, where defined. [5 marks]
questions.explanation: LHS = (sin 3θ cos θ - cos 3θ sin θ) / (sin θ cos θ) [2] = sin(3θ - θ) / (½ sin 2θ) [2] = sin 2θ / (½ sin 2θ) = 2 (RHS) [1].

questions.questionText:
Series — Method of Differences:
Use partial fractions to express 1 / [r(r + 2)] cleanly and hence find ∑_{r=1}^n 1 / [r(r + 2)] in simplified form, stating its limit as n → ∞. [6 marks]
questions.explanation: 1/[r(r+2)] = ½[1/r - 1/(r+2)] [2]. Telescoping sum leaves first two positive and last two negative terms: ½[1 + 1/2 - 1/(n+1) - 1/(n+2)] = 3/4 - ½[1/(n+1) + 1/(n+2)] [3]. As n → ∞, sum → 3/4 [1].

questions.questionText:
Matrices & Eigenvalues/Linear Systems:
Determine all values of k for which the system x + y + z = 3, 2x - y + 3z = 4, 3x + ky + 4z = 7 does NOT have a unique solution. [4 marks]

Roots of Polynomials (Vieta's Relations):
Cubic x³ - 4x² + 7x - 2 = 0 has roots α, β, γ. Find the exact values of (a) α + β + γ, (b) α² + β² + γ², and (c) 1/α + 1/β + 1/γ. [5 marks]
